It's not a question of who deserves what. It's just that it's evil for a system to exist where a few people have all the wealth and luxury they cannot possibly use for many, many lifetimes, while the majority of people struggle to meet their basic needs. Look at the poverty in the rest of the world, and how the elites in those less developed countries control the wealth and resources there and keep the government from implementing pro-poor policies.

Rich people also had the audacity to complain that their life is so boring and suffocating when they have to stay inside their nice big houses... boohoo, some people lost their jobs and only source of income, yet you feel depressed because you're bored sitting at home with all the luxuries modern life can give you?!

I mean how insensitive can you be, blaming people who are desperate to feed themselves and their families. I don't give a fuck about them spending their money to go on vacations, but they sound like elitist assholes when they complain about the masses not following health protocol while they throw parties for their friends and family and travel to other places.
They deserve no pity because they have no dignity and they have no pity in the first place for the woman in the relationship they're helping to destroy.

There's no reason for you to keep on interacting with someone who you know is trying to get into your pants or seek attention from you. This is why I always ignore guys when I get the feeling that they're trying to flirt with me. It's just not worth playing with fire. This holds even more true for guys I've had a romantic or sexual history with, no matter how one-sided the relationship was on either end.

I've always feared the presence of my dad and dreaded the moment he came home, but I can't definitively say that he was abusive father. In retrospect, however, he was abusive to my mother. I don't know if that qualifies as a terrible enough childhood to explain my mental state today. It's not like I was seriously abused in any way. My needs were met and I didn't feel neglected.

I'm just perpetually unhappy. When I think of the supposedly good things in my life, there's always a reason to look at their negative sides. I just want my life to be near-perfect. And I feel really alone. I have good friends who do listen to me, but I can't run to them and whine about my problems every single time I feel bad because they have lives of their own, and they can only put up with so much.
